title: Java's switch fall-through bug -- and how to kill it
description:
One missing `break` in a classic Java switch statement silently falls through to the next case -- a bug that's tripped up developers for decades. Java 14's switch expression with arrow syntax fixes it for good: no fall-through, and it hands back a value directly. Quick look at both, straight from the Control Flow lesson.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-1/03-control-flow/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Forget a single break in a Java switch statement, and your code doesn't error -- it silently falls through into the next case.

display.heading: The switch bug nobody warns you about

beats.narration: Here's the classic switch: three cases, three breaks. Miss just one, and execution keeps running into the next branch -- a bug that's bitten Java devs for decades.
Java 14 gives you a fix: the switch expression. Arrow syntax, no fall-through possible, and it returns a value directly into your variable.
Run it, and you get exactly what you'd expect -- Wednesday. No break needed, no bug waiting to happen.
That one keyword swap makes your branching logic safer by default. Full lesson and code are linked below.
